sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State; Shri Santosh Kumar Singh,
learned counsel for the informant and perused the record.
2.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0066 of 2024, under Section 376(3), 452, 323,
504, 506 IPC & Section 3/4(2) of POCSO Act, P.S. Kumarganj, District Ayodhya.

3. In terms of the FIR lodged on 20.04.2024 it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was alone at home on 05.12.2023 when the applicant came inside the house and after use of force,
committed wrong on her.

Subsequently, statements under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., were recorded Pravesh Kumar vs Statte Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. /Addl. ... on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188913460/
1 which reiterated the FIR version.

entities.text: Pravesh Kumar vs Statte Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. /Addl.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also stated in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that the applicant wanted to marry her by use of force and was threatening to marry her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argues that prior to the lodging of the FIR, a compromise had taken place in which it was agreed that the applicant and the victim would marry.
It is also stated that after garlanding, allegedly, the marriage was also solemnized and the FIR was lodged despite the compromise, after a considerable delay.

5. In terms of the order passed by this Court on 09.07.2024, learned AGA has produced the medical done on 20.04.2024, which naturally did not corroborate the allegation nor does the same record that the victim was pregnant.
The said medical report handed over across the Bar is taken on record.

6. Considering the inordinate delay in lodging the FIR without there being any explanation whatsoever, the applicant who is in custody since 23.04.2024 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Pravesh Kumar be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
